correctness.rationale: For \(p\nmid R\), nonvanishing of the homogeneous resultant implies that \(F=G=0\) has no projective solution modulo \(p\), hence only the affine origin. Thus a primitive coordinate pair has no common value prime outside \(R\). At primes dividing \(R\), homogeneity makes simultaneous vanishing invariant under unit rescaling. CRT gives the exact finite local density, and Möbius inversion over coordinate gcd gives the count with \(O(X\log X)\) error. The only external algebraic input is the standard defining property of the homogeneous resultant; finite calculations are corroborative only.

value.rationale: Homogeneous binary forms with nonzero resultant are a canonical arithmetic class. The resultant exactly isolates the exceptional primes, while homogeneity converts every other common value divisor into coordinate nonprimitivity. The theorem therefore gives a computable finite local correction, covers indefinite forms excluded by the motivating positivity hypothesis, and provides a reusable quantitative count rather than an arbitrary finite slice or numerical recomputation.
